writeup: TIC 200647864 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 12.013960 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The primary eclipse produces a 5.33% dimming, while the secondary eclipse remains undetected. Pixel-level image analysis confirms the signal originates from the target location, with a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 18.3, though the centroid offset of 3.7 arcsec warrants further investigation. The detection achieves a BLS signal-to-noise of 330.6, and the candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs. However, alternating eclipses differ significantly in depth, suggesting the true orbital period is twice the initial automated measurement - a pattern requiring attention in any future observations of this system.
